claim_anchors.finding: Four families are organized by how latent structure is regulated. The review explicitly connects objectives, uncertainty, generative behavior and failure modes.
VAE posterior approximation and weighted ELBO are described, together with representative objectives for other families. These are reviewed formulations rather than new tail-estimation theorems.
The review compares reconstruction/control, sampling effort, stability, collapse modes and distribution-mismatch robustness. This directly overlaps the broader organizing motivation of our synthesis.

claim_anchors.finding: The model retains q(z,c|x)=q(z|x)q(c|x). Categorical weights use a prior-density responsibility approximation, with one-hot known labels where supplied; beta is also adapted for unlabeled data.

Student recognition uses a common chi-square scale and an approximate differentiable Wilson–Hilferty transform. The text calls for clipping near zero precision; its Gaussian limit is the motivation for the approximation.

The divergence surrogate requires nu1 > 2 because it uses Student covariance. Setting identical parameters, nu=3, d=4 gives C1=3,C2=7/3,d1=112/15 and surrogate 154/15, while exact self-KL is zero. An independent mathematical review verified the printed-page algebra.
Mixture-to-standard-Gaussian regularization is approximated through pairwise divergences and carries separate repulsive/attractive weights. These change the objective beyond a mere prior replacement.

Seven-activity sensor sequences,75/25 train/test split,50% labels used during training, latent dimension 4 and 7 components, minimum df 3, two 50-unit GRUs, fixed-scale Laplace/L1 reconstruction. Fifty trials assess the VaDE variants.
Accuracy and qualitative latent topology support this application under its protocol. The source itself calls for validation on more dataset types; no universal clustering guarantee follows.

claim_anchors.finding: Student noise is a Gaussian–Gamma mixture with nu=2c and scale=sqrt(d/c). Each observation has an independent precision. c,d are point-estimated rather than assigned the same factorized Bayesian treatment as remaining variables.
Mean-field separates regression weights, their precisions and observation precisions. Coordinate factor updates are Gaussian/Gamma; short conjugate-gradient steps update c,d by increasing the bound.
The authors explicitly state that true likelihood need not increase when the bound is optimized; if it does not, the bound must become tighter.

claim_anchors.anchor: p132, Fig4 and final paragraph of Section4.1
claim_anchors.finding: The paper observes greater tail-shape estimation error as noise becomes more Gaussian, with improvement from more data; this is relevant antecedent evidence and should not be presented as an unexplored empirical phenomenon.

GCA has independent source distributions and separate precision t_n^(j) for each source/data pair. The source and precision factors are separated as Q(S)Q(T), whereas each Gaussian source vector can have full covariance.

MEG source-separation illustration and discussion support adaptive heavy-tailed versus Gaussian components. The model cannot represent sub-Gaussian independent components; this is a stated scope restriction.

records.review_inference_or_limitation: Section3.2 selects latent dimension and regularization using test accuracy, so its highest-run results are not comparable to fixed-protocol mean-ARI evaluation. These observations concern printed formulas and stated evaluation, not released-code behavior.

claim_anchors.finding: The generative model is p(x,z,c)=p_theta(x|z)p(z|c)p(c). Recognition components are separate diagonal Gaussians; q(z,c|x) retains component dependence. Eq6 is a valid joint ELBO for fixed recognition factors.

EM-V1 uses a prior-only partial assignment criterion; EM-V2 includes the recognition-density denominator but excludes component reconstruction. For fixed model and component recognition, the full objective requires reconstruction plus log prior mass minus component KL in its categorical softmax.

The product contains r_k^L in the denominator, so solving a sample-average criterion requires an Lth-root/geometric-mean score. Printed updates lack that power. This general-L issue is immaterial to the reported L=1 setting stated on p6.
A beta coefficient weights the joint KL. Hard assignment replaces the weighted component sum; these modified training choices must be distinguished from the unweighted soft ELBO.

Prediction uses component encoder means with categorical assignment or a fitted full-covariance GMM. The text reports 20 GMM initialization iterations and selection by best clustering performance. Test labels select latent dimension and beta schedules, and the highest-accuracy training run among five is reported.

The authors report favorable selected ACC for annealed soft EM-V2 on most datasets and state that post-hoc GMM generally performs better than native posterior assignments. These are published-protocol outcomes, not reproduced or pooled benchmark evidence.
